name: Resilient and Connected Appalachians Grant Program
summary: Grants of up to USD 100,000 for land and easement acquisition projects that permanently conserve climate-resilient, connected lands in the Appalachians. The third annual round has closed.

eligibility.rule: Is a conservation nonprofit, 501(c)(3) Indigenous-led group, federally recognized Tribe, or local/state government
Project is within TNC's Appalachians Program boundary
Project includes land partly or fully within the Resilient and Connected Network
Project is within or intersects a focal area
Multiple parcels have one owner and, if non-adjacent, a clear conservation relationship
Project closes on or after April 1, 2027
Applicant submits only one application per year

documents: Project budget, including budget worksheet and narrative
Conflict Inquiry form, if a nonprofit
Current accreditation letter, if an accredited land trust
Letter of Intent for accreditation, if applicable
Organizational by-laws and articles of incorporation
Most recent Form 990 or financial statement

status.quote: Applications open November 12, 2026 and are due by 11:59 PM on January 22, 2027

administered_by.quote: The Nature Conservancy's (TNC) Resilient and Connected Appalachians Grant Program offers funding opportunities

applicant_types.quote: Grants of up to $100,000 are available to land trusts and other non-profit 501(c)(3) organizations with a conservation-related mission, academic institutions, Federally Recognized Tribal Nations

geography.quote: The program geography includes all or portions of Maine, Vermont, New Hampshire, Massachusetts, Connecticut, New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Ohio, Maryland, West Virginia, Virginia, Kentucky, North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee, Georgia and Alabama.

access.quote: The application is completed and submitted through SurveyMonkey's Apply platform.

pool.quote: The total amount of funding this year is at least $1 million.

effort.quote: Applications open November 12, 2026 and close January 22, 2027.

eligibility.quote: The program is open to all land trusts and other non-profit organizations that have conservation-oriented missions, as well as local, county, state government entities and Federally Recognized Tribal Nations. Indigenous-led organizations with 501(c)3 status are also eligible.

Projects must be located in TNC's Appalachians Program boundary which includes portions of Maine, Vermont, New Hampshire, Massachusetts, Connecticut, New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Ohio, Maryland, West Virginia, Virginia, Kentucky, North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee, Georgia or Alabama.
Projects must include lands that fall partly or fully within the Resilient and Connected Network.
Projects must be within or intersect with a focal area.

Yes, if they are adjacent to one another and under a single ownership. If they are not adjacent, the project is still eligible so long as they are owned by the same individual(s) or entity and there is a clear conservation relationship between them
The earliest a project can close and still be eligible for a grant is April 1, 2027.
Applicants may only submit one application per year.

after_award.quote: Grantees must send a copy of the recorded deed to Matt Levy at mlevy@tnc.org no later than 60 days from the date of closing.

documents.quote: Maps and other project-specific attachments Project budget (including budget worksheet and narrative in the application)
The Conflict Inquiry form is required for all non-profit organizations.
Land trusts that are accredited by the Land Trust Accreditation Commission must provide documentation showing that they are and will remain accredited through the start of the grant term.
Letter of Intent for accreditation submitted within the past year (if applicable)
IRS determination letter § Organizational by-laws and articles of incorporation § Most recent Form 990 or Financial Statement § Certificate of Good Standing from State where organization is located
